key_insight: NEXT combines neuro-spectral PDE representations with exponential time differencing to handle stiffness while reducing spectral bias and preserving stability.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more reliable machine-learning solver for stiff forward and inverse PDE problems in scientific computing and physics-based simulation.
method: Represent the PDE solution in a spectral neural architecture (NeuSA-style).
Integrate the stiff linear component exactly using matrix exponentials.
Learn the nonlinear remainder with a neural network and higher-order exponential time differencing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmark tests on multiple stiff PDEs where NEXT remained stable and accurate, while NeuSA diverged; it also worked on inverse problems with sparse data.
watch_item: Matrix-exponential time stepping may increase implementation complexity and computational cost, especially for large stiff systems.
paper_title: NEXT: Physics-Informed Neuro-Spectral Exponential Time Differencing Architectures
